title: session-friction-lane-hypotheses-jot
content:
Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing feature owners ask for a way to reduce end-user friction when backend load spikes or when model costs need to be constrained per-session. Current fallbacks are coarse (global model downgrade or rate-limit) and create bad UX.
- Idea: introduce 'friction lanes' per session: lightweight per-session policies that trade fidelity/cost for latency and availability in a predictable way. Think of them as QoS bands for conversational sessions.

Hypothesis:
- If we allow apps to attach an ordered set of friction lanes to a session (e.g., high-fidelity -> trimmed -> quick-summary -> micro), we can reduce P95 latency and tail-induced costs without increasing user-visible failure modes.

Rough feature sketch (user-facing):
- API: session.create { friction_lanes: ["high", "trim", "summary", "micro"] } with optional per-lane constraints (max_tokens_budget, max_latency_ms)
- Console: session view with active lane and visual indicator showing current lane and recent lane switches
- SDK helpers: decorators to recommend lane sequences based on prompt template and budget

User stories / acceptance criteria:
- As a product engineer, I can attach a friction lane policy to a session so that the runtime can switch lanes automatically when latency/backpressure triggers fire. (AC: create + update calls succeed; policy is visible in session metadata)
- As an SRE, I can set global thresholds that bias lane selection (AC: threshold toggles in Console and an event stream for lane switches)
- As a QA, I can replay a session with injected node latency and verify the system migrates to cheaper lanes within X ms (AC: test harness exists and fails if no lane switch)

Runtime considerations (brain notes):
- Lane semantics map to model variants + prompt transforms + caching profile. Example: 'trim' = shorter context window + prefix drop + quantized model variant; 'summary' = first summarize last N turns then regenerate; 'micro' = constrained token cap and shorter beam/temperature.
- Need deterministic fallback ordering and idempotent lane transitions. Record lane switch events with reason codes.
- KV cache interplay: lane switch may change KV keys (different tokenizer or compression) — must map old KV to new lane when safe, or warm new lane with cached prefixes.
- Routing: prefer local warm nodes for lower latency; fallback to regional cheaper pools when cost-saver lane is selected.

Metrics to track:
- Per-session: lane timeline, average latency per lane, cost per token per lane, timeseries of lane switches
- Experiment metrics: retention delta when lane policy enabled vs control, 95th/99th latency improvements, cost savings per 1k sessions

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: Internal dogfood only — create API + event logging + naive runtime that maps lanes to existing model tags (no prompt transforms yet). Run 2-week test on internal bot.
- Phase 1: Add prompt transforms for 2 lanes (high -> trimmed) and automated thresholding by queue length and latency SLO. Expose toggle in Console.
- Phase 2: Expand lane library and introduce lane packing for multiplexed sessions. Public beta with opt-in flag.

Open questions / risks:
- How to define safe lane transforms that preserve critical semantics (e.g., legal/medical apps) — need per-tenant allowlist and signal for quality regression.
- Billing model: do we bill by actual tokens produced, or also by reserved budget for lanes? Need finance input.
- Complexity of KV migration could add CPU overhead; may negate latency wins if not engineered carefully.
- UX clarity: we must avoid leaking too much implementation detail; show simplified status to app devs with toggle to expand details.

Next steps (short checklist):
- Sync with applied-ml to define lane-to-model mapping and safe transform library (owner: Marcus)
- Draft JIRA epic with gating criteria and experiment plan (owner: Nikhil)
- Quick Console mock for session detail with lane timeline (owner: Lena)
- Prototype lightweight runtime hook to emit lane-switch events and honor policy (owner: SRE small)

Notes to self:
- Keep this lightweight for the first iteration. Avoid building a full DSL for lane policies; start with ordered arrays+simple constraints.
- Think about adding a 'session-importance' flag that biases lane aggression (user-level business importance).

Rough timeline estimate: 8-12 weeks to internal dogfood MVP if we reuse existing model tags and routing primitives.

Brain dump ends — returning to hack on the prototype code.
